paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole stretch teaches me: a person who loves God's word still needs God to come find him. The writer calls before dawn, he praises seven times a day, he says Your law is "my delight," and he still ends by crying out for help (Psalm 119:147, 164, 174). He isn't asking God to notice a perfect record. He's a man who knows he needs the LORD every single hour.

And look at what he holds onto when the pressure builds. Rulers persecute him and his foes are many, yet he says, "The entirety of Your word is truth, and all Your righteous judgments endure forever" (Psalm 119:160, 157). The world keeps changing, and God's word doesn't move. He also says, "Abundant peace belongs to those who love Your law; nothing can make them stumble" (Psalm 119:165). That peace doesn't come from an easy life. It comes from standing on something that lasts.

Then comes the last verse of the longest psalm: "I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments" (Psalm 119:176). I love that, baker. Even after all that devotion, he doesn't say "look how far I've come." He asks to be sought. I know what it is to be stuck in the dark and then found, and I'm still thanking the One who reached in. So keep loving the word, keep calling out, and keep asking Him to seek you. The story of Psalm 119 is over, but your baking in the word is just getting started.
